5. A new device: flash with ESPHome over USB the first time. A device
   already running an older build (local note): no USB needed, and nothing
   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

l5. A new device: flash with ESPHome over USB the first time. A device
   already running an older build (local note): no USB needed, and nothing
   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

e5. A new device: flash with ESPHome over USB the first time. A device
   already running an older build (local note): no USB needed, and nothing
   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   already running an older build (local note): no USB needed, and nothing
   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

k5. A new device: flash with ESPHome over USB the first time. A device
   already running an older build (local note): no USB needed, and nothing
   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   already running an older build (local note): no USB needed, and nothing
   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

o5. A new device: flash with ESPHome over USB the first time. A device
   already running an older build (local note): no USB needed, and nothing
   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local

   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.

   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

a5. A new device: flash with ESPHome over USB the first time. A device
   already running an older build (local note): no USB needed, and nothing
   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

#5. A new device: flash with ESPHome over USB the first time. A device
   already running an older build (local note): no USB needed, and nothing
   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

g5. A new device: flash with ESPHome over USB the first time. A device
   already running an older build (local note): no USB needed, and nothing
   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local

   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.

   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

n5. A new device: flash with ESPHome over USB the first time. A device
   already running an older build (local note): no USB needed, and nothing
   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

 5. A new device: flash with ESPHome over USB the first time. A device
   already running an older build (local note): no USB needed, and nothing
   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   no verdict.

o5. A new device: flash with ESPHome over USB the first time. A device
   already running an older build (local note): no USB needed, and nothing
   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from

   no verdict.

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   no verdict.

:5. A new device: flash with ESPHome over USB the first time. A device
   already running an older build (local note): no USB needed, and nothing
   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

S5. A new device: flash with ESPHome over USB the first time. A device
   already running an older build (local note): no USB needed, and nothing
   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

e5. A new device: flash with ESPHome over USB the first time. A device
   already running an older build (local note): no USB needed, and nothing
   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   already running an older build (local note): no USB needed, and nothing
   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

l5. A new device: flash with ESPHome over USB the first time. A device
   already running an older build (local note): no USB needed, and nothing
   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

 5. A new device: flash with ESPHome over USB the first time. A device
   already running an older build (local note): no USB needed, and nothing
   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

d5. A new device: flash with ESPHome over USB the first time. A device
   already running an older build (local note): no USB needed, and nothing
   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   resets. `partitions.csv` keeps nvs, where every saved setting lives, at
   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.

   the old table's address. Install a build with the `ota:` block's
   `allow_partition_access: true` first (any build, old partition table),
   then send the new table over the air and then the new firmware:

   ```
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --partition-table --device litterbox.local
   esphome upload litterbox-monitor.yaml --device litterbox.local
   ```

   The device checks the table before writing anything and copies the
   running firmware into a slot that exists in the new table if it has to.
   The table write itself takes a few seconds; a power cut during it needs
   a USB flash to recover. Don't skip the journal: the device only keeps
   the last seven minutes of a visit in RAM and reads the rest back from
   it, so without the partition a longer visit is still counted but gets
   no verdict.
